query: For high-entropy nanoalloys in high-temperature applications, what governs structural and chemical stability, and why? Formulate one testable mechanistic hypothesis, propose a controlled comparison that would distinguish it from alternatives, predict observations relative to a baseline, define the boundaries of the prediction, identify supporting evidence from the background, and state a falsifying outcome.

generation.hypothesis: In high-entropy nanoalloys exposed to high temperatures in oxidizing environments, increasing the aluminum content above a critical threshold (>15 at%) promotes the rapid formation of a continuous, adherent Al₂O₃ surface scale that (together with high configurational entropy) suppresses elemental interdiffusion and grain coarsening, thereby enhancing both structural and chemical stability.
generation.material_initial_state: Nanocrystalline equiatomic Cr–Fe–Co–Ni–Al high‐entropy alloy with Al content varied between 5 at% and 25 at%, average grain size ~50 nm.
generation.intervention: Isothermal oxidation in air at 800 °C for 100 h.
generation.conditions: Static air, 800 °C ± 5 °C, 100 h dwell, cooling in air.
generation.structural_mediator: Continuity and thickness of the α-Al₂O₃ surface layer; average grain size after exposure.
generation.mechanism: Above ~15 at% Al, selective outward diffusion of Al and its rapid oxidation form a continuous Al₂O₃ barrier that limits further oxygen ingress and Al depletion. Concurrently, high configurational entropy lowers chemical potential gradients and slows atomic diffusion, suppressing grain growth and phase separation.
generation.predicted_outcome: Alloy with ≥15 at% Al will exhibit a thin (≤1 μm), continuous Al₂O₃ scale, <10% mass gain, and <20% grain coarsening. Alloy with <15 at% Al will form patchy mixed oxides (Cr₂O₃/Fe oxides), >30% mass gain, and >50% grain coarsening.
generation.baseline: 5 at% Al high‐entropy nanoalloy under identical oxidation conditions.
generation.boundary: Valid for Al concentrations between 10 at% and 30 at% and temperatures 700–900 °C in oxidizing atmospheres; not applicable under reducing or cyclic oxidation.
generation.uncertainty: Threshold Al content for continuous scale formation may vary by ±2 at%; quantification of diffusion retardation by configurational entropy is approximate.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two Cr–Fe–Co–Ni–Al nanoalloys (5 at% and 20 at% Al), oxidize both at 800 °C for 100 h in static air. Characterize oxide scale continuity (SEM/EDS), mass gain (thermogravimetry), and grain size (TEM) after exposure.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the 20 at% Al alloy does not form a continuous Al₂O₃ scale or does not show both lower mass gain and suppressed grain growth compared to the 5 at% Al alloy, the hypothesis is falsified.
